project.title: Co-Enhancement of Cellulose Anaerobic Digestion for Methane Production by Zero-Valent Iron and Magnetite at the Transition Temperature-Metagenomic Sequencing
project.description: This study investigated the co-enhancement of methane production from cellulose substrates during anaerobic digestion, utilizing zero-valent iron and magnetite at the transitional temperature. The results indicated that the combined strategy significantly enhanced methane production, with the two iron-based materials promoting the methanogenesis process through distinct mechanisms. This system primarily enriched Firmicutes hydrolytic acidogenic bacteria and Methanosarcina methanogen. A beneficial symbiotic relationship was established between the bacteria and archaea, leading to a high-efficiency interaction within the microbial community that enhanced network connectivity. Furthermore, the enhanced expression of genes involved in various methanogenesis pathways ensured a dynamic equilibrium among different methanogenic routes within the system, ultimately leading to effective energy conservation and emission reduction.
